sourceEvidence.label: P0-A production control source review and approved V1 target

assessment.summary: The reviewed source supports one structural opportunity: remove operator-owned checkout bytes from production root execution while retaining internal Git, Registry, release evidence, exact-commit release state, and four RepoDigests. The selected design uses one root-authorized full tracked-tree snapshot per commit and is not production-validated.

nonNegotiables: Retain the internal Git mirror, private Registry, release-evidence store, controlled bridge, remote driver, lifecycle lock, and existing release state machine.
Every production Registry commit requires a root-owned root:root 0444 marker containing exact ASCII <commit>\n before host-control adoption.
The root snapshot is the complete regular Git-tracked tree under versions/<40hex commit>; current is the only active host-control fact.
Ordinary release prepare, activate, and status continue to bind exact commit, release evidence, and four image RepoDigests without a control digest or manifest-schema change.
Host-control adoption and bootstrap are independently approved OS changes even when the release driver orchestrates host-control commands.
Precreate fixed production env, secret, approval, and security-report paths with reviewed owner/mode changes.
Do not add a selective control closure, fifth image, OCI control artifact, privileged release daemon, new signing schema, Kubernetes or datastore HA, or an expanded offline package.
Preserve recovery_required, compensation, forward-only schema behavior, and forward rollback.
Do not treat this analysis as production work or successful validation.
assumptions: The approved V1 target places internal Git, Registry, release evidence, monitoring, redacted logging, and encrypted backup storage on one Ops VM.
Core, PostgreSQL, and the broker/auth/control Redis instances remain on one accepted non-HA production VM.
The fixed revision's complete regular tracked tree is 1000 files and 17750771 bytes; later candidate revisions remain within reviewed hard bounds.
Existing schema-v1 Registry manifests and schema-v2 offline compatibility readers remain exact and are not extended for host-control fields.
nonGoals: Provision or modify production, pre-production, the Ops VM, Registry, internal Git, evidence store, monitoring, logging, or backup infrastructure.
Eliminate the accepted single-production-VM or single-Ops-VM failure domains.
Replace the application release state machine or introduce automatic schema/control downgrade.
Claim KMS, HSM, HA, disaster recovery, or security closure from design documents or unverified working-tree code.

opportunities.title: Bind production root execution and runtime artifacts to one approved commit
opportunities.summary: Move privileged repository execution out of the operator checkout and require a root-authorized current snapshot at the exact release commit before the unchanged four-RepoDigest lifecycle runs.
opportunities.diagnosis: The current checkout owns both daily Git updates and bytes later parsed, imported, or executed with root/Docker authority. An arbitrary local 40-hex commit is not root authorization because the operator can write local .git; the release identity therefore needs a separate root approval marker and immutable commit snapshot.

evidence.claim: The production wrapper derives managers and Compose files from its checkout root; the host asset contract installs the wrapper as a symlink into that checkout and root systemd units contain direct checkout execution paths.
The remote release driver performs operator-side Git fetch and fast-forward before invoking privileged release prepare, activate, and status.
The release manager and store already enforce exact commit/image/migration identities, terminal recovery_required, compensation, and forward-only schema handling.
D041 defines RepoDigest promotion as the intended identity path and D094 describes the signed offline archive as temporary compatibility infrastructure with an explicit Registry exit condition.
The Phase 0 threat model records Core, PostgreSQL, and three Redis domains on one common production VM and does not claim HA.
The approved V1 target retains internal Git and Registry/evidence channels and binds a root-owned full tracked-tree snapshot to the same exact commit as the four RepoDigests.

The approved KISS constraint requires a root-owned per-commit approval marker and rejects a selective closure, control digest, manifest field, fifth image, OCI control artifact, new daemon, signing change, Kubernetes/HA, and offline expansion.

Because root entry points resolve executable or policy bytes from the operator-updateable tree, operator compromise or error can plausibly influence root and Docker behavior even when the release manifest and images remain exact.
Because the operator can write local Git metadata, a syntactically valid commit alone cannot grant root execution authority; a root-controlled allow decision must precede snapshot activation.

desiredInvariants: Every production root process executes repository bytes only from one complete root-owned versions/<40hex commit> generation.
The stable launcher takes the existing lifecycle lock before resolving current and pins one verified physical generation for the operation.
Host-control prepare, activate, status, launcher, and bootstrap require a root:root 0444 single-link approval marker containing exactly the 41 ASCII bytes <commit>\n.
The normal wrapper, release manager, operator, and containers cannot create or repair approval markers.
Current is the only active host-control fact; approval markers authorize commits but never select the active generation.
Every snapshot manifest records exact commit, Git tree, and every regular tracked file's path, Git mode, size, and SHA-256; missing, extra, linked, or drifted entries fail closed.
The ordinary release lifecycle and signed manifest schema remain unchanged and bind exact commit, immutable release evidence, and four image RepoDigests.
The driver orders marker-gated host-control prepare/activate/status before ordinary release prepare/activate/status for production Registry releases.
Production env, canonical secrets, approval markers, and security-report state use fixed precreated OS paths with exact owner/mode contracts.
Application compensation never silently rolls schema or active control backward; different-commit host activation requires the current commit to be a Git ancestor of the candidate.
The offline reader remains compatibility-only and receives no host-control payload or automatic fallback role.
Single production and Ops VM failures remain explicitly non-HA residual risks.

options.title: Root-owned full release tree
options.summary: Replace the operator-owned active checkout with one root-owned full tree at the exact approved commit.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Root ownership removes the operator-checkout write-to-root path after every entry is migrated.
The operator Git workflow no longer mutates the active tree, requiring a redesigned source/data workflow.
The existing state machine can remain, but full-tree identity and forward-control behavior need integration.
Registry promotion and offline exit are required regardless of active tree ownership.
Changing tree ownership does not remove the accepted single-VM failure domain.
It can bind exact commit and images but over-couples application data/Git and OS release.
It avoids new daemons/artifacts but still needs root commit authorization and a broader OS operating model.

tradeoffs.assessment: One root-owned active tree removes the observed checkout ownership edge and makes the trusted repository surface explicit.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Tamper with every former checkout root entry and prove root always resolves the verified OS-owned tree.

tradeoffs.assessment: No SMS request-path hop is added; full-tree hashing/copy occurs during OS adoption.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure full-tree plan/apply duration and require completion within the approved OS window.

tradeoffs.assessment: No resident process is introduced, although retained full trees consume disk.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure peak verification RSS and retained-generation disk.

tradeoffs.assessment: Atomic tree publication can improve crash behavior, but broad Git/data/persistence migration adds failure modes.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Inject failures across full-tree publication and data migration; require one complete active tree or fail closed.

tradeoffs.assessment: The familiar operator checkout and application-only release model are replaced by a broad OS-managed tree.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Classify representative releases and rehearse operator workflows under the new tree model.

tradeoffs.assessment: Git, staging, configuration, persistence, ownership, systemd, and release paths need coordinated redesign.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Complete a pre-production cutover/reversal rehearsal without changing application data or schema.

residualRisks: The full active tree is a large root trusted computing base.
OS and application release become operationally coupled.
Schema and control still cannot be automatically downgraded after activation side effects.

workPackages: Implement full active-tree ownership and commit authorization.
Migrate configuration, persistence, and systemd entry points.
acceptanceCriteria: No production root entry resolves to operator-writable bytes.
Atomic full-tree switch survives interruption without a mixed tree.
Application release preserves exact commit and forward-only schema behavior.
After first activation, the full tree remains on the same commit or advances only to a marker-authorized Git descendant; prior and divergent trees are never reactivated.
migrationNotes: Prefer only if the operator checkout will be removed from production.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Before first activation, abandon the staged tree without changing the active root. After activation, never reactivate a prior or divergent tree; repair with a separately approved descendant and use existing application recovery.

options.title: Commit-keyed full tracked-tree snapshot
options.summary: Keep operator Git evidence but execute privileged repository bytes from a complete root-owned versions/<commit> tree authorized by a root marker and selected only by current.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Every privileged entry moves to the root-owned snapshot; complete tracked-tree coverage avoids selective-closure omissions.
Operator Git supplies exact bytes/evidence, while the root marker authorizes and the snapshot supplies execution.
The existing lifecycle remains the sole application recovery authority; current is the sole active host-control fact.
The design adopts Registry RepoDigest promotion and keeps offline support compatibility-only.
The accepted production common failure domain remains.
The same exact commit identifies internal Git, the current root snapshot, release evidence, and the four images.
The root marker supplies authorization without a daemon, fifth artifact, control digest, or new state machine.

tradeoffs.assessment: The design removes checkout bytes from root execution, copies the complete tracked tree, and prevents the operator from authorizing arbitrary local commits without a root marker.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run checkout, local-Git, marker, environment, systemd, snapshot, and Registry/evidence tamper matrices; require fail-closed behavior before side effects.

tradeoffs.assessment: No resident process or SMS request-path hop is added; the fixed baseline hashes/copies 1000 files and 16.93 MiB only during OS adoption/status checks.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure marker, plan, first prepare, idempotent prepare, activate, status, and ordinary release wall time against pre-production baselines.

tradeoffs.assessment: The design adds root-owned files and transient verification buffers, not a resident process, queue, or cache.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure peak RSS and retained snapshot disk for the refreshed implementation revision.

tradeoffs.assessment: Complete commit generations and one atomic relative current link yield deterministic interruption outcomes; marker authorization is stateless read-only validation.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Inject failures before/after snapshot fsync, current replacement, launcher replacement, and every release transition.

tradeoffs.assessment: Phase 0 requires one independently approved root marker and host-control adoption for every production Registry commit, plus fixed-path metadata review.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Rehearse marker creation, driver plan, absent-marker rejection, snapshot adoption, ordinary release, and marker/snapshot retention cleanup.

tradeoffs.assessment: The launcher, snapshot/marker contracts, control/data root split, systemd paths, fixed OS metadata, and driver ordering require coordinated changes while application/schema contracts remain unchanged.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Deliver reviewable work packages and complete pre-production bootstrap, idempotent retry, rollback, Registry release, reboot, backup, and restore rehearsals.

residualRisks: A missed privileged entry can still re-enter the operator checkout even though the snapshot is complete.
The stable launcher, bootstrap, snapshot manager, marker OS process, and full tracked tree are a high-value root TCB.
A mistakenly approved malicious commit is faithfully root-executable; approval does not prove code correctness.
Ops VM or bridge compromise can correlate Git, Registry, evidence, monitoring, and backup failures if identities and keys are not separated.
The production and Ops VMs remain non-HA common failure domains.
Complete production-host root compromise can expose mounted secrets without KMS/HSM.

workPackages: Freeze exact full-tree, marker, path, and size contracts.
Validate exact 41-byte <commit>\n root markers in prepare, activate, status, launcher, and bootstrap without exposing approval mutation.
Build and verify complete versions/<commit> generations from fixed Git objects.
Make current the only atomic active fact.
Bootstrap manager/snapshot/current first and stable launcher last with idempotent retry.
Precreate and preview fixed platform env, secrets, approval, and security-report owner/mode contracts.
Preserve the signed manifest and ReleaseStore state while splitting control and data roots.
Order Registry host-control adoption before the unchanged release lifecycle.
Reroute production systemd root entry points.
Complete pre-production security, crash, resource, release, backup, and restore validation.
acceptanceCriteria: Every marker-authorized commit snapshot exactly equals its complete regular Git-tracked tree and canonical manifest.
Current is always a safe relative link to versions/<commit> and is the only active host-control fact.
The operator, normal wrapper/release actions, and containers cannot create approval markers; wrong owner, mode, link count, size, or <commit>\n content fails closed.
No root production entry executes or imports operator-checkout bytes.
Fixed production env, secrets, approval, and security-report paths match reviewed owner/mode/type contracts.
Driver host-control prepare, activate, and status completes for the exact commit before unchanged release prepare, activate, and status.
Same-commit host activation is idempotent; every different activated commit is a marker-authorized Git descendant, while backward and divergent transitions fail closed.
No control digest, manifest field, host state, intent, journal, daemon, or installer state machine exists.
Existing recovery_required and forward-only schema behavior remains unchanged.
Internal Git, Registry, and release evidence remain; offline is compatibility-only.
migrationNotes: Every Phase 0 production Registry commit incurs a lightweight independently approved root marker and OS adoption.
Historical offline packages remain compatibility/audit inputs and are not extended.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Host control never activates a prior or divergent commit. Same-commit retry is idempotent; repair activates a separately approved descendant while application images use existing compensation/recovery.

options.title: Privileged release agent and separate control artifact
options.summary: Introduce an Ops orchestrator, production root daemon, privileged protocol, and independently promoted control artifact.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: A daemon can own privileged code, but becomes a new root attack surface.
Local operator Git can be removed from release authority, requiring a new protocol and identity model.
Daemon state must reconcile with ReleaseStore before forward-only guarantees can be assessed.
Registry can carry a control artifact, but that expands artifact/signing contracts.
A release agent does not change the single production VM failure domain.
The agent can join identities but replaces the approved local driver/lock boundary with a larger system.
The option conflicts with KISS prohibitions on a daemon, fifth/OCI artifact, and signing changes.

tradeoffs.assessment: A narrow service can centralize authorization, but adds a network-reachable root parser, credential, and protocol lifecycle.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Threat-model and independently review authentication, authorization, replay, parsing, upgrade, and root capability boundaries.

tradeoffs.assessment: Every release operation gains an orchestrator/agent protocol hop and serialization, though application traffic is unaffected.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Benchmark end-to-end release operations against the direct-driver baseline.

tradeoffs.assessment: A resident daemon, request buffers, credentials, queues, and observability state consume persistent resources.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure idle/peak RSS, queue bounds, and replay recovery memory.

tradeoffs.assessment: Central coordination can help a fleet, but daemon/ReleaseStore state and orchestrator availability create new ambiguous failures for one host.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Inject partitions, duplicate requests, crashes, orchestrator loss, upgrade mismatch, and ReleaseStore conflict.

tradeoffs.assessment: The option requires daemon lifecycle, certificates, protocol compatibility, monitoring, and another privileged deployment channel.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Produce and rehearse install, upgrade, key-rotation, and incident runbooks before reconsideration.

tradeoffs.assessment: It replaces the approved driver boundary and expands Registry, evidence, signing, and host installation contracts.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Require a separate architecture review and prototype; do not combine with P0-A.

residualRisks: The privileged network daemon becomes a high-value remote attack surface.
Daemon and ReleaseStore state can diverge.
A new control artifact/signing path can drift from the four-image release identity.
The option does not remove single-VM or Ops VM failure domains.

workPackages: Complete a separate architecture and threat-model review.
migrationNotes: Defer unless a measured multi-host coordination need appears.

opportunities.recommendation: Use a stable root-owned launcher plus one root-authorized complete tracked-tree snapshot per exact production commit. The root marker authorizes, current alone selects, the driver orchestrates the OS sub-change, and the ordinary four-RepoDigest release lifecycle remains schema-compatible.

openQuestions: Which two-person OS approvers create and retire root-owned commit markers?
What snapshot/marker retention floor covers the active commit, recovery_required evidence, and forensic/audit needs when inactive generations are not rollback targets?
Are numeric service IDs 10001 and 101 frozen on the production host for the security-report owner/mode contract?
Which production root systemd units are allowed and which test/development units must be absent or masked?
What measured pre-production time, RSS, and disk thresholds fit the OS maintenance window?
Which identities write and read the internal Git, Registry, and release-evidence channels?
